reviewer_summary.question: Why can a chatbot process the known prompt together but choose its answer only one token at a time?
reviewer_summary.takeaway: The next choice depends on processing the token just chosen, while cached intermediate results let the model reuse earlier work.

findings.problem: Blue's new numbers could mean its input list, its new key, or its new value: those are the numbers I have seen so far. I cannot identify which numbers get compared with the keys, so I may conclude that blue's key is what performs the comparison. The picture shows resulting weights without showing the missing comparison input.

resolution.note: Names blue’s fresh query and displays the actual query vector as comparison input; shows the resulting computed weights across all four values. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: The grid cells previously represented transformed position outputs; now those same cells contain two saved lists. Nobody says how the two lists relate to the output list I was following, or when they were made during prefill. I may mistake the cached pair for the complete output of a layer.

resolution.note: Adds a reuse roadmap, explains two extra lists derived from layer inputs during prefill; unlabelled saved bars appear before their K/V names. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: Layer two uses saved results, blue produces final scores, and the model chooses and in one beat. I have just followed a layer-one attention mixture, but its feed-forward operation and the result becoming layer two's input are skipped here. I cannot trace which fresh result moves upward to produce the next scores.

resolution.note: Added fb_ffn to show layer-one transformation and its fresh output going into layer two before next scores. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: The prediction asks about one pass through all the layers before I know what a layer is or what happens in a pass. I understand the question about parallel calculation, but cannot picture the condition I am being asked to predict.

resolution.note: Prediction now asks about choosing two answer pieces, without requiring prior understanding of layers or passes. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: After learning that blue must go back through the model, I suddenly start learning about saved numeric pairs. The narration has not said that we are now answering how the model processes blue while reusing the prompt's work, so I lose why this new mechanism belongs in the explanation.

resolution.note: Adds a reuse roadmap, explains two extra lists derived from layer inputs during prefill; unlabelled saved bars appear before their K/V names. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: One beat introduces mixing, attention, an independent transformation, and a feed-forward network while three numeric states appear. Both transitions also include an unexplained residual operation in their labels. I cannot tell which changes demonstrate the two stated jobs and which come from the extra operation.

resolution.note: Actual computed vectors show input and attention result. Feed-forward now has its own separate beat and result; residual terminology moved out of the core. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: The crossed arrow goes from is to blue, although the earlier blocked connection ran from a later input to an earlier output. If these arrows still show information flowing between positions, the picture now seems to forbid blue from using is. The direction needs a clear meaning for the causal explanation to hold together.

resolution.note: Forbidden information-flow edge now runs from later blue INPUT toward earlier is OUTPUT, matching the earlier mask illustration. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.

findings.problem: The saved lists are concrete, but deciding the mix remains abstract: I hear about comparing keys and mixing values before seeing either operation on those lists. I have names for two lists without yet being able to explain their different jobs.

resolution.note: Concrete lists are named with their two jobs, followed by the query and actual computed mixing weights. Subsequent fresh read required; this edit is not acceptance.
